record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
record.original_question: Study and classify all 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of Eⁿ⁺², where 2-type means that the position vector field has a spectral decomposition x = c + x₁ + x₂ with Δx₁ = λ₁x₁ and Δx₂ = λ₂x₂ for two distinct eigenvalues λ₁ and λ₂. In particular, classify the 2-type hypersurfaces of the hypersphere S⁴ in E⁵.

evidence.quote: if all of the eigenvalues λ1,...,λk associated with the spectral decomposition are mutually different, then the immersion x (or the submanifold M) is said to be of k-type.
Problem 2. Study and classify 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere of E^(n+2). In particular, classify 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere S4 in E^5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E^{n+2}$ denote the $(n+2)$-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard inner product and Laplacian $\Delta$ acting componentwise on vector-valued functions. Let $S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$ be a round hypersphere, and let $x: M^n \to S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected orientable $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold as a hypersurface of $S^{n+1}$.

The immersion $x$ is said to be of $2$-type if the position vector field admits a spectral decomposition
$$x = c + x_1 + x_2,$$
where $c\in E^{n+2}$ is a constant vector and $x_1, x_2: M \to E^{n+2}$ are non-constant smooth maps satisfying
$$\Delta x_1 = \lambda_1 x_1, \qquad \Delta x_2 = \lambda_2 x_2,$$
for two distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_1 \ne \lambda_2$.

Problem. Classify, up to rigid motions of $E^{n+2}$, all $2$-type hypersurfaces $M^n$ of $S^{n+1}\subset E^{n+2}$. In particular, give a complete classification of all $2$-type hypersurfaces of the unit $4$-sphere $S^4 \subset E^5$.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere are known to have constant nonzero mean curvature and constant scalar curvature, and several local rigidity and partial classification theorems (including the classification of 2-type surfaces in S^3 as products of two circles of distinct radii) have been established. However, a complete classification of 2-type hypersurfaces in S^{n+1} for general n, and specifically in S^4, does not appear to have been achieved; the problem is still listed as open in recent surveys on finite-type submanifolds.

status_evidence.title: 2-TYPE SURFACES IN A HYPERSPHERE
status_evidence.snippet: A hypersurface of a hypersphere S^{n+1} is of 2-type iff it has constant nonzero mean curvature and constant scalar curvature (with exceptions).
status_evidence.claim: Characterization but not full classification of 2-type hypersurfaces in hyperspheres is known.

status_evidence.title: Local rigidity theorems of 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere
status_evidence.snippet: Local rigidity theorems of 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (local rigidity) results are available; full classification remains open.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys finite-type submanifolds including 2-type hypersurfaces and lists open classification problems.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of 2-type hypersurfaces in hyperspheres remains an open problem.
